```{r, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
options(width = 110)
library(sciparseR)
ex <- function(f) system.file("extdata", f, package = "sciparseR")
has_ocr <- requireNamespace("tesseract", quietly = TRUE) &&
  "eng" %in% tesseract::tesseract_info()$available
```

The core of sciparseR needs no OCR, no model files and no external
service. This article covers the three optional extensions and states
exactly what each one does in this version.

## OCR

Scanned pages have no text layer. sciparseR detects them (ink on the
rendered page, no words) and marks them `ocr_status = "needed"`. With
`ocr = "auto"` and the tesseract package installed, those pages are
rendered to a temporary image and recognized; `ocr = "always"` replaces
the text layer of every page.

```{r, eval = has_ocr}
doc <- sc_parse(ex("scanned.pdf"), config = sc_config(ocr = "auto", ocr_language = "eng", ocr_dpi = 300))
sc_pages(doc)[, c("page", "image_only", "ocr_status")]
sc_blocks(doc, page = 2)[, c("type", "method", "status", "text")]
doc$spans[doc$spans$source == "ocr_tesseract", c("text", "x0", "y0", "x1", "y1", "confidence")][1:6, ]
doc$warnings[, c("stage", "code", "message")]
```

OCR words become spans with `source = "ocr_tesseract"`, boxes mapped to
page points, and the recognizer's own confidence (0 to 100). That number
is tesseract's score, not a calibrated probability: a page with a low
median confidence gets an `ocr_low_confidence` warning, and OCR blocks
carry `status = "ocr"` so they can be treated with care downstream. Note
the recognition error "Is" for "is" in the output above: OCR text should
be reviewed.

If tesseract is not installed, the page is marked `unavailable` with a
warning; parsing never fails because OCR is missing.

## ONNX models

Learned models (layout detection, table structure recognition, formula
recognition) can handle what geometry cannot. sciparseR prepares for them
without pretending they are integrated:

* **No automatic downloads.** You obtain a model file yourself.
* **Registry with license and checksum.** `sc_model_register()` refuses a
  model until you accept its license, records the SHA-256, and
  `sc_onnx_session()` checks it again every time.
* **Raw inference** through [nativeORT](https://github.com/calebmcarr/nativeORT)
  with `sc_onnx_infer()`.

```{r}
reg <- file.path(tempdir(), "models")
f <- tempfile(fileext = ".onnx")
writeBin(as.raw(seq_len(64)), f)
sc_model_register("demo-layout", f, task = "layout", license = "MIT",
                  accept_license = TRUE, source = "local file", registry = reg)
sc_models(reg)[, c("name", "task", "license", "sha256")]
sc_onnx_status()[c("available", "integrated_tasks", "note")]
```

`integrated_tasks` is empty: in this version no learned model is used by
`sc_parse()`. Detection models such as Table Transformer return several
tensors (class logits and boxes) and `nativeORT::ort_infer_raw()`
returns only the first, so the boxes cannot be decoded. Parsing therefore
always uses the geometric methods, and the documentation says so rather
than advertising a capability that does not work end to end.

```{r}
sc_model_remove("demo-layout", registry = reg)
```

## GROBID

[GROBID](https://github.com/kermitt2/grobid) is a mature service for
header metadata and references. sciparseR never calls it. If you run it
yourself, read its TEI output and compare:

```{r}
tei <- tempfile(fileext = ".tei.xml")
writeLines(c(
  '<TEI xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0"><teiHeader><fileDesc><titleStmt>',
  '<title level="a" type="main">Effect of Drug A on Blood Pressure: a Synthetic Example</title>',
  '</titleStmt></fileDesc></teiHeader><text><body>',
  '<div><head n="1.">Introduction</head></div><div><head n="2.">Methods</head></div>',
  '<div><head n="3.">Results</head></div></body><back><listBibl>',
  '<biblStruct xml:id="b0"><analytic><title level="a">Global burden of hypertension</title>',
  '<idno type="DOI">10.1000/jsm.2020.001</idno></analytic>',
  '<monogr><title level="j">J Synth Med</title><imprint><date type="published" when="2020"/></imprint></monogr>',
  '</biblStruct></listBibl></back></text></TEI>'), tei)
g <- sc_read_grobid(tei)
g$references
sc_compare_grobid(sc_parse(ex("single_column.pdf")), g)
```
